A Salesforce Developer Edition announcement describes Hosted MCP as included at no cost in that edition.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The best-matched documented SObject All server has read tools (schema, query, find, identity, recent records, related records), create/update tools, and delete tools. Official standard-server docs say standard tool sets are fixed. Tool annotation fields are not shown in the SObject reference pages reviewed; Tableau Next pages do publish readOnlyHint and openWorldHint for that different server. 2. Delete docs say to confirm with the user and recommend query/review first; they do not document a server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval workflow. 3. OAuth 2.0 and PKCE are documented; operations run as the authenticated Salesforce user and respect object permissions, field-level security, and sharing rules. Standard servers are disabled by default and require administrator activation. Client callback URLs and External Client App setup are required. Token lifetime/revocation details were not found. 4. Separate standard endpoints include production and sandbox/scratch. SObject Reads, Mutations, Deletes, and All provide different fixed operation sets; standard tool sets cannot be modified. Custom servers permit administrator selection/configuration of exposed capabilities. No endpoint query-parameter tool filter was found. 5. SObject access follows Salesforce object permissions, field-level security, sharing rules, validation rules, and record relationships. The reviewed docs do not describe MCP-specific PII masking. 6. SObject All SOQL is documented with a 50,000-record transaction cap; SOSL search returns at most 2,000 records. SObject docs advise WHERE/LIMIT and indexed-field filtering. Data 360 API calls consume underlying API limits and Flex Credit usage; this is a different server. 7. Schemas expose field details and validation constraints; docs say invalid/missing required fields, permissions, and validation failures can cause operations to fail. No MCP-specific argument correction or operator override behavior was documented. 8. Salesforce states updates appear in the authenticated user's audit trail. MCP-specific logging configuration, retention, and telemetry details were not found. 9. No feedback/rating/survey/report-to-vendor tool was identified in the 11-tool SObject All list. 10. Natural-language prompt templates are described; delete confirmation and query-first guidance are text recommendations. No server instructions were published for the unspecified endpoint. 11. No evidence found that prior agent behavior changes future tools or results. 12. The hosted offering is a family of distinct standard and configurable custom endpoints, not one universal flat tool list. The exact input endpoint is unspecified. 13. SOQL and SOSL accept query/search strings but are not arbitrary REST request or script execution tools in the documented SObject All list.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The selected SObject All reference documents core record CRUD, queries, search, schema, identity, and relationship operations; it does not establish which other Salesforce UI, API, analytics, or administrative features are available in the unspecified endpoint's org. Salesforce's REST APIs and product UI expose broader functionality, but comparing the unknown endpoint to the full product would require its actual server path and org configuration. Within SObject All, no undelete MCP tool is available; users may recover deleted records from the Recycle Bin for up to 15 days.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Delete documentation says: “Confirm with the user before deleting.” It also instructs agents to query and review the target set before delete and present results for approval “when possible.” The SObject All reference recommends WHERE and LIMIT clauses for SOQL. These are documented agent-use instructions; the pages do not describe a server-enforced confirmation field or query-shape gate.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Salesforce states that “every transaction runs as the authenticated user” and that existing CRUD, field-level security, and sharing rules apply. Its announcement says an agent cannot perform operations the authenticated user lacks permission to perform, and updates appear under that user's name in the audit trail. Setup requires OAuth and PKCE. These are documented platform claims; the public hosted implementation is unavailable for code-level verification.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The service is described as Salesforce-managed infrastructure with no server provisioning or uptime management for customers. Hosted MCP servers are generally available for Enterprise Edition orgs and above. Standard servers must be activated by an administrator and have fixed tool sets.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The endpoint reference and GA announcement document per-user authentication and platform permission enforcement, but hosted server code is not public, so implementation-level enforcement could not be independently inspected. Delete confirmation, query-first review, and query-filter guidance are text instructions in the docs. Salesforce describes audit trails but does not document MCP-specific log retention or configuration in the reviewed sources.

contradictions: The input says a per-customer endpoint exists based on manufacturer documentation but does not provide a concrete URL or server path. Salesforce documents multiple standard and custom hosted endpoints; therefore /platform/sobject-all is used only as best available endpoint evidence, not confirmed as the input endpoint.

Salesforce's official documentation separately lists many hosted server variants and product capabilities. They are not interchangeable tool lists; actions.json uses the official 11-tool SObject All reference only and does not combine other server tools.

The supplied OAuth evidence says metadata was not fetched because the input endpoint is not concrete. Salesforce docs describe OAuth, PKCE, and setup scopes, but endpoint-specific OAuth metadata and a complete supported-scope list cannot be compared to the tool list.
observations_for_research: Salesforce provides distinct standard endpoint paths for different operation scopes, including read-only, mutation, delete-focused, and full CRUD variants; administrators activate standard servers but cannot modify their tool sets.
The hosted offering also supports org-configured custom servers, so the available MCP surface can depend on administrator configuration as well as the endpoint path.
Published delete confirmation and query-first guidance is phrased as an instruction to the agent; the reviewed docs do not describe server-side confirmation enforcement.

Salesforce's per-user identity and permission model links MCP operations to existing org permissions and audit identity, while Data 360 and other product servers can bring additional licenses, permission sets, or usage accounting.
